(By Sri. K. Krishna Kumar, Hcgp For R1;

 This Crl.P Is Filed U/S 439(2) Cr.Pc Praying To
Cancel The Anticipatory Bail Granted To The
Respondent No.2 To 7 By The Xlv City Civil And
Sessions Judge, Bangalore In Criminal
Misc.No.1821/2023 By Order Dated 03.03.2023 Vide
Annexure A.
 This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The complainant/victim is before this Court in this petition under Section 439(2) of Cr.P.C. seeking cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to respondent Nos.2 to 7/accused Nos.1 to 6 by the learned Sessions Judge in Crl.Misc. No.1821/2023.

2. Heard both the sides and perused the material on record.
3.

Crime No.20/2023 was registered at East Zone Women Police Station on a complaint lodged by the petitioner herein against respondent Nos.2 to 7 for offences punishable NC: 2023:KHC:19165 under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC' for short) and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (hereinafter referred to as 'DP Act' for short).
4. The Learned Sessions Judge was pleased to enlarge the accused on anticipatory bail vide order dated 03.03.2023 imposing conditions.

5. The grievance of the petitioner is that, she was not given an opportunity to oppose the prayer seeking bail, though she filed a application under Section 301(2) of Cr.P.C., to assist the prosecution.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the order was obtained by suppressing the real facts and therefore, it is necessary to hear the petitioner/complainant.

He would rely on a decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Jagjeet Singh and Others V/s. Ashish Mishra and Others (Crl.A. No.632/2022) decided on 18.04.2022, to contend that the victim has a legally vested right to be heard at every step post the occurrence of an offence.

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 would contend that, only after hearing the Public Prosecutor and after considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case and after assigning proper reasons, the learned Sessions Judge has granted anticipatory bail.
He submits that there is no suppression of facts as alleged.
He therefore, seeks to reject the petition.
8. A perusal of the material on record shows that the petitioner/de-facto complainant - victim in this case filed an application under Section 301(2) read with Section 438 of Cr.P.C. on 28.02.2023.
A memo dated 02.03.2023 was filed seeking adjournment till next day for filing objections on the ground that the certified copies of the petition was applied but it was not received.
The learned Sessions judge allowed the application filed under Section 301(2) of Cr.P.C. and the de- facto complainant was permitted to assist the prosecution.

But when the matte was listed on 02.03.2023,
memo filed on behalf NC: 2023:KHC:19165 of the complainant seeking adjournment till next day was rejected and the order granting anticipatory bail was passed on 03.03.2023 allowing the petition.
9. It is no doubt true that, the learned Sessions Judge has considered in detail the facts and circumstances of the case and passed a well considered order.
However, justice must not only be done, but must be seen to be done.
10. In the present case, victim's application for assisting the prosecution was though allowed, but a short adjournment sought by the petitioner was rejected.
It is settled that that the victim has a right to participate in criminal proceedings.

In the light of the above decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court relied on by the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Sessions Judge ought to have given an opportunity for the complainant to oppose the petition.

In that view of the matter, learned Sessions Judge may have to be directed to hear the parties afresh on the petition seeking anticipatory bail, giving a fair opportunity to the petitioner to file objection and oppose the petition.

Hence, the following:
NC: 2023:KHC:19165 ORDER 1) Order dated 03.03.2023 passed in Crl. Misc.
No.1821/2023 by the Court of XLV Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City (CCH-46) is hereby set aside.

entities.text: Court of XLV Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City (CCH-46)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2) The learned Sessions Judge is directed to hear the parties afresh and dispose of the petition within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
3) Till the disposal of the said petition, the accused shall have the benefit of anticipatory bail granted by the learned Sessions Judge.
4) All the contentions are kept open.
5) Petition is disposed of.
